entries.reflection: God says through Isaiah, remember not the former things, nor consider the things of old. Sometimes we must let go of the past to see something new.
studyPrompts: What former thing are you holding on to?
What would letting go look like?
What new thing might you be missing?

entries.passageText: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that I have set before thee life and death, the blessing and the curse; therefore choose life, that thou mayest live, thou and thy seed;
entries.reflection: I have set before you life and death; therefore choose life. The Torah's call is clear: life is precious and worth choosing. If you are struggling, reach out today.
studyPrompts: What helps you choose life?
Who reminds you that your life matters?
What makes you feel alive?

entries.passageText: Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are home-born in Israel shall dwell in booths; that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.
entries.reflection: On Sukkot Israel dwells in temporary booths to remember the journey through the wilderness. Holidays in temporary places have a long history.
studyPrompts: What holidays will you spend away?
How could you mark them where you are?
What does a temporary dwelling teach you?

entries.passageText: And the LORD, He it is that doth go before thee; He will be with thee, He will not fail thee, neither forsake thee; fear not, neither be dismayed.’
entries.reflection: Moses told Joshua the LORD goes before you, will be with you, and will not fail or forsake you. Transitions are easier when we know we are not alone.
studyPrompts: What transition are you facing?
What does it mean that God goes before you?
Who goes with you?

entries.passageText: O magnify the LORD with me, And let us exalt His name together.
entries.reflection: O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt His name together. Praise is meant to be shared.
studyPrompts: Whom do you pray or praise with?
How could you gather with others?
What could you celebrate together?

entries.passageText: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee, And before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee; I have appointed thee a prophet unto the nations.
entries.reflection: God tells Jeremiah, before I formed you I knew you, and appointed you. A calling can be older than our awareness of it.
studyPrompts: What do you feel called to?
How did you discover it?
How could you honor it today?

entries.passageText: And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him; male and female created He them.
entries.reflection: God created humanity in His image, male and female. Every person, including you, carries that image and its worth.
studyPrompts: What does being made in God's image mean to you?
Where do you doubt your worth?
How could you honor God's image in others?

entries.passageText: He restoreth my soul; He guideth me in straight paths for His name's sake.
entries.reflection: He restores my soul. The shepherd of Psalm 23 restores the weary. Restoration is God's work.
studyPrompts: What needs restoring in you?
What restores your soul?
Where have you been restored before?

entries.passageText: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.
entries.reflection: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable to You. This verse closes the Amidah. Contemplation shapes speech.
studyPrompts: What do you meditate on?
Are your words and thoughts aligned?
How could you make this prayer your own?

entries.passageText: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise; And he that shutteth his lips is esteemed as a man of understanding.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says even a fool who keeps silent is counted wise. Silence can be wisdom.
studyPrompts: When is silence wise for you?
Where do you talk too much?
What could silence teach you?

entries.passageText: He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; But he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says one who is slow to anger has great understanding. Forbearance is a sign of wisdom.
studyPrompts: What makes you quick to anger?
What would slowing down look like?
Who models patience for you?

entries.passageText: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed: ‘The LORD, the LORD, God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth;
entries.reflection: The LORD proclaimed Himself merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in goodness and truth. These Thirteen Attributes are central to Jewish prayer.
studyPrompts: Which of these attributes speaks to you?
Where have you known God's grace?
How could you reflect it?

entries.passageText: Then I was by Him, as a nursling; And I was daily all delight, Playing always before Him, Playing in His habitable earth, And my delights are with the sons of men.
entries.reflection: Wisdom says she was beside God as a nursling, playing always before Him and delighting in humanity. Delight and play are part of creation.
studyPrompts: When do you feel delight?
What would playful joy look like?
How could you make room for it?

entries.passageText: Tell ye your children of it, And let your children tell their children, And their children another generation.
entries.reflection: Joel tells the people to tell their children, and their children's children. Memory is handed down generation to generation.
studyPrompts: What stories were passed to you?
What will you pass on?
Whom could you tell?

entries.passageText: For He knoweth our frame; He remembereth that we are dust.
entries.reflection: God knows our frame and remembers that we are dust. God's compassion is shaped by knowing our limits. You can be gentle with yourself for the same reason.
studyPrompts: Where are you hard on yourself?
What limits do you need to accept?
How could you show yourself compassion?

entries.passageText: He that goeth about as a talebearer revealeth secrets; But he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth a matter.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says a talebearer reveals secrets, but the faithful in spirit conceal a matter. Trustworthiness keeps confidences.
studyPrompts: Who trusts you with secrets?
Do you keep them?
Whom do you trust?

entries.passageText: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says to open your mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy. Speaking up is part of justice.
studyPrompts: Whose cause could you plead?
Where are you silent when you should speak?
What would speaking up cost you?

entries.passageText: And he said: ‘Let me go, for the day breaketh.’ And he said: ‘I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.’
entries.reflection: Jacob wrestled through the night and said, I will not let you go unless you bless me. Persistence can bring blessing.
studyPrompts: What are you wrestling with?
What blessing are you seeking?
What helps you hold on?

entries.passageText: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says one with a generous eye is blessed, for they share their bread with the poor. Sharing begins with how we see.
studyPrompts: What do you have to share?
Whom could you share with?
How do you see those in need?

entries.passageText: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
entries.reflection: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. Psalm 23 speaks of needs met.
studyPrompts: What do you need?
What do you want that you may not need?
How has God provided?

entries.passageText: For He is our God, And we are the people of His pasture, and the flock of His hand. To-day, if ye would but hearken to His voice!
entries.reflection: Today, if you would but hearken to His voice. The psalm calls us to listen now, not later.
studyPrompts: What might you be called to hear today?
What are you postponing?
How could you listen now?

entries.passageText: Only for God wait thou in stillness, my soul; For from Him cometh my hope.
entries.reflection: The psalmist tells his soul to wait in stillness for God, for from Him comes hope. Expectation rests in God.
studyPrompts: What are you hoping for?
Where does your hope come from?
What would waiting in stillness look like?

entries.passageText: And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places, Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; And thou shalt be called The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.
entries.reflection: Isaiah promises that those who care for others will rebuild old ruins and be called the repairer of the breach. Rebuilding is holy work.
studyPrompts: What breach needs repairing?
What ruins could you rebuild?
Who could help you?

entries.passageText: My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me, and art far from my help at the words of my cry?
entries.reflection: My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? The psalmist laments openly. Honest lament is part of faith.
studyPrompts: What is your lament?
Can you say it to God?
Who could hear it with you?

entries.passageText: Seven days shalt thou keep a feast unto the LORD thy God in the place which the LORD shall choose; because the LORD thy God shall bless thee in all thine increase, and in all the work of thy hands, and thou shalt be altogether joyful.
entries.reflection: The Torah commands seven days of rejoicing at Sukkot, for God blesses the work of your hands, and you shall be altogether joyful. Rejoicing is commanded.
studyPrompts: What blessings could you rejoice in?
How could you celebrate?
Whom could you rejoice with?

entries.passageText: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in Him, and He will bring it to pass.
entries.reflection: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will act. Commitment and trust go together.
studyPrompts: What way are you on?
What would committing it to God look like?
Where is trust hard?

entries.passageText: The heart is deceitful above all things, And it is exceeding weak—who can know it?
entries.reflection: Jeremiah says the heart is deceitful above all things; who can know it? We can fool ourselves. Honesty with ourselves takes humility.
studyPrompts: Where might you be fooling yourself?
Who helps you see clearly?
What truth do you avoid?

entries.passageText: Cast thy bread upon the waters, For thou shalt find it after many days.
entries.reflection: Cast your bread upon the waters, for you will find it after many days. Generous risk can return in time.
studyPrompts: What risk could you take?
What are you afraid to let go?
What returns have you seen from risk?

entries.passageText: And thus shall ye eat it: with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste—it is the LORD’s passover.
entries.reflection: Israel ate the first Passover with loins girded, shoes on and staff in hand, ready to go. Readiness was part of redemption.
studyPrompts: What are you preparing for?
Are you ready to move?
What would readiness look like now?

entries.passageText: Show me Thy ways, O LORD; teach me Thy paths. Guide me in Thy truth, and teach me; For Thou art the God of my salvation; For Thee do I wait all the day.
entries.reflection: Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths. The psalmist asks for guidance every day.
studyPrompts: Where do you need guidance?
How do you ask for it?
Whom has God used to guide you?

entries.passageText: With my soul have I desired Thee in the night; Yea, with my spirit within me have I sought Thee earnestly; For when Thy judgments are in the earth, The inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
entries.reflection: Isaiah says, with my soul I have desired You in the night. Longing for God often comes in the dark hours.
studyPrompts: What do you long for at night?
What does that longing tell you?
How could you bring it to prayer?

entries.passageText: Be strong and of good courage, fear not, nor be affrighted at them; for the LORD thy God, He it is that doth go with thee; He will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.’
entries.reflection: Be strong and of good courage, fear not, for the LORD your God goes with you; He will not fail you. Grit is fed by knowing you are not alone.
studyPrompts: What requires courage from you now?
What does God's presence mean to you?
Who goes with you?

entries.passageText: Arise, shine, for thy light is come, And the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee.
entries.reflection: Arise, shine, for your light has come. Isaiah calls Israel to rise at the dawn of redemption.
studyPrompts: What new light do you see?
What would arising look like?
How could you shine for others?

entries.passageText: Who is among you that feareth the LORD, That obeyeth the voice of His servant? Though he walketh in darkness, And hath no light, Let him trust in the name of the LORD, And stay upon his God.
entries.reflection: Isaiah says that one who walks in darkness, with no light, should trust in the name of the LORD and rely on God. In dark times, trust and reach for help.
studyPrompts: What darkness are you walking in?
What would trust look like?
Who could walk with you?

entries.passageText: Will two walk together, Except they have agreed?
entries.reflection: Amos asks, can two walk together unless they have agreed? Harmony needs shared direction.
studyPrompts: Whom do you walk with?
Where do you disagree?
How could you find agreement?

entries.passageText: I have set the LORD always before me; Surely He is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
entries.reflection: The psalmist says, I have set the LORD always before me; I shall not be moved. Conviction steadies the soul.
studyPrompts: What do you set before you?
What moves you off course?
How could you hold steady?

entries.passageText: And God saw every thing that He had made, and, behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
entries.reflection: God saw all He had made, and it was very good. Creation's order is called good.
studyPrompts: Where do you see good order?
Where is your life disordered?
What would bring order?

entries.passageText: NUN. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, And a light unto my path.
entries.reflection: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. When things are confusing, the next step can still be lit.
studyPrompts: What confuses you?
What light do you have for the next step?
Who helps you see?

entries.passageText: ’Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep’— So shall thy poverty come as a runner, And thy want as an armed man.
entries.reflection: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands, and poverty comes. Sloth works slowly.
studyPrompts: Where are you putting things off?
What small step could you take?
What would diligence look like?

entries.passageText: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house; thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.
entries.reflection: You shall not covet your neighbor's house or anything that is your neighbor's. The last commandment guards the heart against greed.
studyPrompts: What do you covet?
What would contentment look like?
How could you be glad for others?

entries.passageText: Thou openest Thy hand, And satisfiest every living thing with favour.
entries.reflection: You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor. Desires find their fulfillment in God's generosity.
studyPrompts: What do you desire?
How has God satisfied you?
What desire needs reshaping?

entries.passageText: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says, if you find honey, eat only what is enough, or you will be sick. Moderation keeps appetite healthy.
studyPrompts: Where do you overindulge?
What is enough?
How could you practice moderation?

entries.passageText: Say not thou: ‘I will requite evil’; wait for the LORD, and He will save thee.
entries.reflection: Do not say, I will repay evil; wait for the LORD, and He will save you. Revenge is left to God.
studyPrompts: Who has wronged you?
What would waiting look like?
How could you let go of revenge?

entries.passageText: Ye shall not steal; neither shall ye deal falsely, nor lie one to another.
entries.reflection: The Torah says, you shall not steal, nor deal falsely, nor lie to one another. Honesty is holiness in daily life.
studyPrompts: Where are you tempted to deceive?
How could you be more honest?
Who models honesty for you?

entries.passageText: Better is a little with righteousness Than great revenues with injustice.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says better a little with righteousness than great income with injustice. Honest gain is worth more.
studyPrompts: Is your gain honest?
What would you give up for integrity?
How do you define enough?

entries.passageText: Comfort ye, comfort ye My people, saith your God.
entries.reflection: Comfort, comfort My people, says your God. Isaiah begins the prophecies of consolation with these words.
studyPrompts: Where do you need comfort?
How has God comforted you?
Whom could you comfort?

entries.passageText: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to bemoan him and to comfort him.
entries.reflection: When Job's three friends heard of his trouble, they came to comfort him. Their first act was to show up and sit with him.
studyPrompts: Who is suffering near you?
How could you show up?
What does good comfort look like?

entries.passageText: The LORD support him upon the bed of illness; mayest Thou turn all his lying down in his sickness.
entries.reflection: The LORD supports the sick on their bed. Caring for the sick, bikur cholim, is a mitzvah in Jewish life.
studyPrompts: Who is sick around you?
How could you visit or help?
Who cared for you when you were sick?

entries.passageText: He doth execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.
entries.reflection: God executes justice for the orphan and widow, and loves the stranger, giving food and clothing. God cares for the vulnerable, and asks us to as well.
studyPrompts: Who is vulnerable around you?
How could you provide for them?
What does God's care teach you?

entries.passageText: If there be among you a needy man, one of thy brethren, within any of thy gates, in thy land which the LORD thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thy heart, nor shut thy hand from thy needy brother;
entries.reflection: If there is a needy person among you, do not harden your heart or shut your hand. Poverty calls for an open hand.
studyPrompts: Who is in need?
Where has your heart hardened?
How could you open your hand?

entries.passageText: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies; Thou hast anointed my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
entries.reflection: You prepare a table before me; my cup runs over. Abundance comes even in hard places.
studyPrompts: Where has your cup overflowed?
What abundance do you overlook?
How could you share it?

entries.passageText: And God blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it; because that in it He rested from all His work which God in creating had made.
entries.reflection: God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it He rested. Shabbat is a gift of rest.
studyPrompts: How do you rest?
How could you keep Shabbat where you are?
What makes rest holy?

entries.passageText: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, And drink thy wine with a merry heart; For God hath already accepted thy works.
entries.reflection: Ecclesiastes says to eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a merry heart. Shared meals can be joyful.
studyPrompts: Whom do you share meals with?
How could a meal become joyful?
Whom could you invite?

entries.passageText: O sing unto the LORD a new song; Sing unto the LORD, all the earth.
entries.reflection: O sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth. Song is part of worship.
studyPrompts: What songs move you?
What new song could you sing?
When do you sing?

entries.passageText: that I will give the rain of your land in its season, the former rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil.
entries.reflection: God promises rain in its season, the early and the late rain. Rain is a blessing.
studyPrompts: What rain do you need?
What seasons have you seen?
How do you give thanks for provision?

entries.passageText: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast; But the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says the righteous regard the life of their animals. Care for creatures is part of righteousness.
studyPrompts: How do you treat animals?
What creature have you cared for?
What does this teach about compassion?

entries.passageText: Yonder sea, great and wide, Therein are creeping things innumerable, Living creatures, both small and great.
entries.reflection: The psalmist marvels at the great wide sea, full of creatures great and small. The sea shows God's wonders.
studyPrompts: When have you seen the sea?
What wonders do you notice?
How does nature move you?

entries.passageText: Thy righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Thy judgments are like the great deep; Man and beast Thou preservest, O LORD.
entries.reflection: The psalmist says God's righteousness is like the mighty mountains. Mountains speak of steadiness.
studyPrompts: What is steady in your life?
What mountains have you seen?
How could you be steady for others?

entries.passageText: The righteous shall flourish like the palm-tree; He shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
entries.reflection: The righteous will flourish like a palm and grow like a cedar of Lebanon. Growth is slow and strong.
studyPrompts: Where are you growing?
What helps you flourish?
What is your cedar?

entries.passageText: And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corner of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleaning of thy harvest; thou shalt leave them for the poor, and for the stranger: I am the LORD your God.
entries.reflection: The Torah says to leave the corners of the field and the gleanings for the poor and the stranger. Harvest includes sharing.
studyPrompts: What is your harvest?
What corners could you leave for others?
Who needs your gleanings?

entries.passageText: Sow to yourselves according to righteousness, Reap according to mercy, Break up your fallow ground; For it is time to seek the LORD, Till He come and cause righteousness to rain upon you.
entries.reflection: Hosea says to sow righteousness, reap mercy, and break up your fallow ground. What we sow shapes what grows.
studyPrompts: What are you sowing?
What fallow ground needs breaking?
What do you hope to reap?

entries.passageText: For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, And that spreadeth out its roots by the river, And shall not see when heat cometh, But its foliage shall be luxuriant; And shall not be anxious in the year of drought, Neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
entries.reflection: Jeremiah compares the one who trusts God to a tree by water, spreading roots and not anxious in drought. Roots hold through hard seasons.
studyPrompts: What are your roots?
What waters them?
How do they help in drought?

entries.passageText: And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver; and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver; and there shall be they that shall offer unto the LORD offerings in righteousness.
entries.reflection: Malachi describes God sitting as a refiner and purifier of silver. Refining is careful and patient.
studyPrompts: What is being refined in you?
How do you endure it?
What is coming out pure?

entries.passageText: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye for water, And he that hath no money; Come ye, buy, and eat; Yea, come, buy wine and milk Without money and without price.
entries.reflection: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters, even without money. Isaiah's invitation is free.
studyPrompts: What are you thirsty for?
What free gift could you accept?
Whom could you invite?

entries.passageText: And a man shall be as in a hiding-place from the wind, And a covert from the tempest; As by the watercourses in a dry place, As in the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
entries.reflection: Isaiah says a person can be a hiding place from the wind and shelter from the storm, like the shade of a great rock. People can be shelter for each other.
studyPrompts: Who shelters you?
Whom could you shelter?
What storms are you facing?

entries.passageText: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
entries.reflection: Grace is deceitful and beauty vain, but one who fears the LORD shall be praised. Appearance fades; character remains.
studyPrompts: How much does appearance matter to you?
What would you like to be praised for?
Whose character do you admire?

entries.passageText: But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, And He that formed thee, O Israel: Fear not, for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name, thou art Mine.
entries.reflection: I have called you by name; you are Mine. To be known by name is to be loved.
studyPrompts: What does being called by name mean to you?
Who knows you well?
How could you know someone better?

entries.passageText: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
entries.reflection: Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching heaven, with angels ascending and descending. Dreams can open our eyes to God's nearness.
studyPrompts: What dreams do you remember?
Where have you sensed God near?
What ladder connects you to heaven?

entries.passageText: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint. Vision gives direction.
studyPrompts: What vision guides you?
Where do you lack vision?
How could you find it?

entries.passageText: Commit thy works unto the LORD, And thy thoughts shall be established.
entries.reflection: Commit your works to the LORD, and your plans will be established. Plans rest on trust.
studyPrompts: What are you planning?
Have you committed it to God?
What would trust look like?

entries.passageText: Make plain the path of thy feet, And let all thy ways be established.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says to make the path of your feet level, and all your ways will be established. Wise decisions take care with each step.
studyPrompts: What decision is before you?
What would a level path look like?
Who could help you decide?

entries.passageText: He that walketh in his integrity as a just man, happy are his children after him.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says the righteous walk in integrity, and their children after them are blessed. Example shapes generations.
studyPrompts: Who sees your example?
What legacy are you leaving?
Whose example blessed you?

entries.passageText: For by Thee I run upon a troop; and by my God do I scale a wall.
entries.reflection: By You I run against a troop; by my God I scale a wall. Overcoming is possible with God's help.
studyPrompts: What wall are you facing?
What would overcoming look like?
Who helps you climb?

entries.passageText: The wicked earneth deceitful wages; But he that soweth righteousness hath a sure reward.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says the one who sows righteousness has a sure reward. Righteousness is never wasted.
studyPrompts: What righteousness are you sowing?
What reward do you hope for?
How do you stay faithful?

entries.passageText: As cold waters to a faint soul, So is good news from a far country.
entries.reflection: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a far country. Letters from home refresh.
studyPrompts: What news from home refreshes you?
Whom could you write to?
What good news could you send?

entries.passageText: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen; and he presented himself unto him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
entries.reflection: Joseph went up to meet his father Israel, fell on his neck and wept a long while. Reunion after long separation brings tears of joy.
studyPrompts: Whom are you longing to see?
What would reunion feel like?
How do you hold hope until then?

entries.passageText: and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood over against him; and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed down to the earth, and said: ‘My lord, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant.
entries.reflection: Abraham saw three strangers, ran to meet them, and bowed, asking them to stay. Hachnasat orchim, welcoming guests, is a central Jewish value.
studyPrompts: Whom could you welcome?
How do you treat guests?
When were you welcomed warmly?

entries.passageText: My flesh and my heart faileth; But God is the rock of my heart and my portion for ever.
entries.reflection: My flesh and heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart forever. Weakness does not have the final word.
studyPrompts: Where do you feel weak?
What strengthens your heart?
Who helps you in weakness?

entries.passageText: Wherefore I perceived that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion; for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
entries.reflection: Ecclesiastes says there is nothing better than to rejoice in one's work. Joy in work is a portion to accept.
studyPrompts: What work do you enjoy?
How could you find joy in your current work?
What makes work meaningful?

entries.passageText: Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.
entries.reflection: Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates. Praise should follow real deeds.
studyPrompts: Whose works deserve praise?
How could you praise them?
What works would you like to be known for?

entries.passageText: And the man said: ‘The woman whom Thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.’
entries.reflection: Adam blamed the woman, and through her, God. Blame shifting is as old as Eden. Taking responsibility breaks the pattern.
studyPrompts: Whom do you blame?
What is your part?
How could you take responsibility?

entries.passageText: Thus saith the LORD: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, Let not the rich man glory in his riches; But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth, and knoweth Me, That I am the LORD who exercise mercy, justice, and righteousness, in the earth; for in these things I delight, Saith the LORD.
entries.reflection: Let not the wise glory in wisdom, nor the mighty in might, nor the rich in riches, but in knowing God, who practices kindness and justice. True glory lies there.
studyPrompts: What do you take pride in?
What would glorying in God look like?
How could you practice kindness and justice?

entries.passageText: Glorify not thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men; For better is it that it be said unto thee: ‘Come up hither’, than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom thine eyes have seen.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says do not put yourself forward before the king; better to be told, come up here. Rank is given, not grabbed.
studyPrompts: Where do you push for position?
What would humility look like?
How do you treat those above and below you?

entries.passageText: Have we not all one father? Hath not one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, Profaning the covenant of our fathers?
entries.reflection: Malachi asks, have we not all one father? Has not one God created us? Equality is rooted in a shared Creator.
studyPrompts: Whom do you treat as less?
What does one Creator mean for how you treat others?
Where is treachery between people?

entries.passageText: Is wisdom with aged men, And understanding in length of days?—
entries.reflection: Job says wisdom is with the aged, and understanding in length of days. Elders carry wisdom.
studyPrompts: What elders have taught you?
What could you ask an older person?
How do you honor elders?

entries.passageText: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; And let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, And walk in the ways of thy heart, And in the sight of thine eyes; But know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
entries.reflection: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, but know that God will bring you into judgment. Youth is for joy and responsibility.
studyPrompts: What did youth teach you?
How do you balance joy and responsibility?
What would you tell a younger person?

entries.passageText: I have more understanding than all my teachers; For Thy testimonies are my meditation.
entries.reflection: The psalmist says he has more understanding than all his teachers, because he meditates on God's testimonies. Good teachers point beyond themselves.
studyPrompts: Who are your teachers?
What have you learned beyond them?
Whom could you teach?

entries.passageText: After the LORD your God shall ye walk, and Him shall ye fear, and His commandments shall ye keep, and unto His voice shall ye hearken, and Him shall ye serve, and unto Him shall ye cleave.
entries.reflection: After the LORD your God shall you walk, keep His commandments and cleave to Him. Following is a daily walk.
studyPrompts: What does following God look like for you?
Where do you struggle to follow?
What helps you cleave to Him?

entries.passageText: And Moses said: ‘I will turn aside now, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.’ And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said: ‘Moses, Moses.’ And he said: ‘Here am I.’
entries.reflection: Moses turned aside to see the burning bush, and only then did God call to him. An interruption became a calling.
studyPrompts: What interrupts your day?
Could something be calling you?
How could you turn aside to look?

entries.passageText: Who can discern his errors? Clear Thou me from hidden faults.
entries.reflection: Who can discern his errors? Clear me from hidden faults. Mistakes we do not see still need forgiveness.
studyPrompts: What mistakes might you not see?
Who could help you see them?
How do you seek forgiveness?

entries.passageText: And Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
entries.reflection: Moses died at one hundred and twenty, his eye not dim nor his strength gone. His story ended with strength intact. Endings can be full.
studyPrompts: What is ending for you?
How could you finish well?
What would a full ending look like?

entries.passageText: Now the LORD said unto Abram: ‘Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto the land that I will show thee.
entries.reflection: God told Abram, go from your land and your father's house to the land I will show you. New places begin with a step of trust.
studyPrompts: What new place are you facing?
What are you leaving?
How could you trust the next step?

entries.passageText: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise; But the companion of fools shall smart for it.
entries.reflection: Proverbs says one who walks with the wise grows wise. Admiration leads us toward those we become like.
studyPrompts: Whom do you admire?
Whom do you walk with?
Whom could you learn from?

entries.passageText: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him, and said unto him: ‘The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.’
entries.reflection: The angel greeted Gideon as a mighty man of valor before Gideon believed it himself. Believing in others can call out their courage.
studyPrompts: Whom could you believe in?
Who believed in you before you did?
How could you tell someone you believe in them?

entries.passageText: And the heaven and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And on the seventh day God finished His work which He had made; and He rested on the seventh day from all His work which He had made.
entries.reflection: The heavens and earth were finished, and on the seventh day God completed His work and rested. Completion leads to rest.
studyPrompts: What have you completed?
What would it mean to rest after it?
What is still unfinished?
